mn82:7.12: “Mum and dad, as I understand the Buddha’s teachings, it’s not easy for someone living at home to lead the spiritual life utterly full and pure, like a polished shell.
mn82:7.13: I wish to shave off my hair and beard, dress in ocher robes, and go forth from the lay life to homelessness.
mn82:7.14: Please give me permission to go forth.”
mn82:7.15: For a third time, Raṭṭhapāla’s parents said to him:
mn82:7.16: “But, dear Raṭṭhapāla, you’re our only child. You’re dear to us and we love you. You’re pampered and raised in comfort.
mn82:7.18: Even when you die we will lose you against our wishes.
mn82:7.19: So how can we allow you to go forth while you’re still alive?”
mn82:8.13: And for a second time, Raṭṭhapāla kept silent.
mn82:8.15: “Dear Raṭṭhapāla, you’re our only child. You’re dear to us and we love you. You’re pampered and raised in comfort.
mn82:8.17: When you die we will lose you against our wishes. So how can we allow you to go forth from lay life to homelessness while you’re still living?
mn82:8.18: Get up, Raṭṭhapāla! Eat, drink, and amuse yourself.
mn82:8.19: While enjoying sensual pleasures, delight in making merit.
mn82:8.20: We don’t allow you to go forth.
mn82:8.21: When you die we will lose you against our wishes.
mn82:8.22: So how can we allow you to go forth while you’re still alive?”
mn82:10.14: “Our dear Raṭṭhapāla, you are the only child of your parents. You’re dear to them and they love you. You’re pampered and raised in comfort. You know nothing of suffering. When you die your parents will lose you against their wishes.
mn82:10.15: So how can they allow you to go forth while you’re still alive?
mn82:10.16: Get up, Raṭṭhapāla! Eat, drink, and amuse yourself. While enjoying sensual pleasures, delight in making merit.
mn82:10.17: Your parents will not allow you to go forth. Even when you die your parents will lose you against their wishes.
mn82:10.18: So how can they allow you to go forth while you’re still alive?”
mn82:38.15: And it was after knowing and seeing and hearing this that I went forth from the lay life to homelessness.”
mn82:38.18: ‘The world is unstable and swept away.’
mn82:39.15: ‘Please, my dear friends and colleagues, relatives and kin, all of you here share my pain so that I may feel less pain.’
mn82:39.19: And it was after knowing and seeing and hearing this that I went forth from the lay life to homelessness.”
mn82:39.22: ‘The world has no shelter and no savior.’
mn82:40.9: ‘I will continue to amuse myself in the same way, supplied and provided with these same five kinds of sensual stimulation.’
mn82:40.13: And it was after knowing and seeing and hearing this that I went forth from the lay life to homelessness.”
mn82:40.16: ‘The world has no owner—you must leave it all behind and pass on.’
mn82:41.25: ‘Please, Great King, you should know this. I come from over the ocean.
mn82:41.26: There I saw a large country that is successful and prosperous, populous and full of people.
mn82:41.27: They have many divisions of elephants, cavalry, chariots, and infantry.
mn82:41.28: And there’s plenty of money and grain,
mn82:41.29: plenty of gold, coined and uncoined, worked and unworked,
mn82:41.30: and plenty of women for the taking.
mn82:41.31: With your current forces you can conquer it.
mn82:41.39: ‘The world is wanting, insatiable, the slave of craving.’
